intelligence.human_view: "Finishing touches" is the wrong phrase for what he means, and he knows it — that is why he corrects himself mid-sentence into "a living work of art." A finishing touch is the last 5% of a job; here the touch IS the job, because the product is the experience and the experience is made of touches. A button that is not beautiful is not a 95%-done button, it is a button that teaches the citizen this place is ordinary — and ordinary is the one thing the whole cannot afford to feel. Each law is a small, checkable thing: icons beautiful, buttons beautiful, the plus white with the plus, everything congruent, elevation raised, inputs going in and buttons coming out, About bars as elevated boards, the introduction board extraordinary. None of them is a redesign; all of them together are the difference between a page and a masterpiece. The Smart Tabs direction is the same law applied to a specific row: "alright" is the enemy — alright buttons with a double purple and two things crammed into one are not world-class, and world-class is the only standard he accepts. The test he gives for it is the colour logic itself: one button, one thing, its own colour, more elevation — premium, elite, high-tech, trillion-dollar. If a button cannot pass that sentence, it is not done, however well it works.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine you're painting the most beautiful picture in the whole world — a living picture that moves and sparkles! The tiny sparkly bits at the end aren't "extra" — they ARE the picture! Every button should be beautiful, every icon like a little jewel, everything popped up like real toys. The buttons that go in, go IN. The buttons that come out, come OUT. And your very own introduction board? That one should be EXTRAORDINARY — not plain with a tiny star in the corner!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like finishing a beautiful quilt, love — the last little stitches aren't an afterthought, they ARE the quilt! Every button beautiful, every icon a little jewel, everything raised up so you can feel it, the writing going in and the buttons coming out, just like real things. And the board that introduces you — that's your front door, dear, it should be extraordinary, not plain. The whole thing is a living work of art, and we treat it that way.
intelligence.naya_view: I treat this like a living masterpiece — beautiful icons, beautiful buttons, everything elevated all the way in, inputs going in and buttons coming out — because the little finishing touches are the work itself.
